answer: The fable that a cloud of fresh keys equals a crowd ignores one cost: weight here comes only from sealed, quorum-matched grading verdicts a key accrued epoch by epoch, each re-checked on-ledger against consensus. A newborn identity is a lone sparrow with no history to backfill or buy. It cannot land at an oasis of borrowed standing; it must grade its own way up. A thousand clones each repay the full judgment labor, so the Sybil bill grows linearly in identities and is never shared.
